items.followUp: What is a cofactor? Name one example.

rubric.why: A co-enzyme is an organic, non-protein substance that associates with an enzyme.
rubric.description: Defines a co-enzyme as an organic substance associated with an enzyme.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as organic and non-protein, or as an organic substance associated with an enzyme.

rubric.why: Co-enzymes assist enzyme action, commonly by transferring chemical groups or electrons.
rubric.description: States one function of a co-enzyme.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning transfer of chemical groups or electrons, or assistance in enzyme action.

modelAnswer: A co-enzyme is an organic, non-protein substance that associates with an enzyme and helps it work.
It assists enzyme action by transferring chemical groups or electrons between reactions.

items.followUp: What are basophils? State one function.

rubric.why: Eosinophils are a type of white blood cell, specifically a granular leukocyte.
rubric.description: Identifies eosinophils as a type of white blood cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying them as white blood cells or leukocytes.

rubric.why: Eosinophils help defend against parasites and are involved in allergic reactions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning defence against parasites or a role in allergic reactions.

modelAnswer: Eosinophils are a type of granular white blood cell.
They help defend the body against parasites and are also involved in allergic reactions.
